cards.title: Building of the Large Pyramids
facts: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom.
It is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one still standing.

cards.title: Foundation of Rome (Legend)
facts: According to legend, Rome was founded by Romulus on April 21, 753 BC.
Romulus became the first king of Rome after killing his twin brother Remus.

cards.title: The Foundation of Athenian Democracy
facts: Cleisthenes introduced democratic reforms in Athens.
This is considered the birth of democracy in Western civilization.

cards.title: Battle of Marathon
facts: The Greeks defeated the Persians in this famous battle.
A messenger ran from Marathon to Athens to announce the victory, inspiring the modern marathon race.

cards.title: Hannibal Crosses the Alps
facts: Hannibal led his army, including war elephants, across the Alps to invade Italy.
This was one of the most daring military maneuvers in ancient history.

cards.title: Cleopatra Coronation to Pharaoh
facts: Cleopatra VII became the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt.
She ruled jointly with her father and later with her brothers and son.

cards.title: Appointment of First Roman Emperor Augustus
cards.image: Appointment of first Roman Emporer Augustus - 27BC
facts: Augustus Caesar became the first Roman Emperor, ending the Roman Republic.
His reign marked the beginning of the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace.

cards.title: Edict of Milan
facts: Constantine I granted religious tolerance to Christianity in the Roman Empire.
This marked a turning point in the history of Christianity.

cards.title: Hijra (Mohammed Exiles to Medina)
facts: The Prophet Muhammad migrated from Mecca to Medina.
This event marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

cards.title: Coronation of Charlemagne
facts: Charlemagne was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III.
This marked the revival of the Western Roman Empire.

cards.title: Coronation of Otto I in Rome (HRE)
facts: Otto I was crowned Holy Roman Emperor, establishing the Holy Roman Empire.
His reign strengthened the connection between Germany and Italy.

cards.title: Walk to Canossa
facts: Emperor Henry IV sought forgiveness from Pope Gregory VII.
This event symbolized the conflict between secular and religious authority.

cards.title: The Fall of Jerusalem (First Crusade)
facts: Crusaders captured Jerusalem from Muslim control.
This led to the establishment of Crusader states in the Holy Land.

cards.title: Magna Carta Libertatum
facts: King John of England signed the Magna Carta, limiting royal power.
It is considered one of the most important legal documents in history.

cards.title: The Plague
facts: The Black Death killed an estimated 25-30 million people in Europe.
It was one of the deadliest pandemics in human history.

cards.title: Invention of the Printing Press by Gutenberg
cards.image: Invention of the Printing Press by Gutenberg - 1440
facts: Johannes Gutenberg invented the movable-type printing press.
This revolutionized the spread of knowledge and information.

cards.title: End of War of the Roses
cards.image: End of War of the Roses - 1487
facts: The civil war between the Houses of Lancaster and York ended.
Henry VII established the Tudor dynasty.

cards.title: Discovery of America
facts: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas, opening the age of exploration.
This marked the beginning of widespread European colonization.

cards.title: Reconquista
facts: The Christian kingdoms completed the reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula from Muslims.
Granada, the last Muslim stronghold, fell to Ferdinand and Isabella.

cards.title: Start of Reformation
facts: Martin Luther posted his 95 Theses, challenging the Catholic Church.
This sparked the Protestant Reformation.

cards.title: The Conquest of the Aztec Empire by Hernán Cortés
cards.image: The Conquest of the Aztek Empire by Hernan Cortes - 1521
facts: Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés defeated the Aztec Empire.
This led to Spanish colonization of Mexico.

cards.title: The Conquest of the Inca Empire by Francisco Pizarro
cards.image: The Conquest of the Inka Empire by Francisco Pizarro - 1532
facts: Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa.
This led to the fall of the Inca Empire.

cards.title: Augsburg Peace of Religion
facts: The Peace of Augsburg allowed German princes to choose between Lutheranism and Catholicism.
This temporarily ended religious conflicts in the Holy Roman Empire.

cards.title: Defeat of Spanish Armada
facts: The English navy defeated the Spanish Armada.
This marked the decline of Spanish naval dominance.

cards.title: Third Defenestration of Prague
facts: Protestant rebels threw Catholic officials out of a window in Prague.
This event sparked the Thirty Years' War.

cards.title: Peace of Westphalia
facts: A series of peace treaties ended the Thirty Years' War.
It established the principle of state sovereignty in international relations.

cards.title: Glorious Revolution and Bill of Rights
cards.image: Glorious Revolution and Bill of Rights - 1689
facts: William III and Mary II became joint monarchs of England.
The English Bill of Rights limited royal power and established parliamentary supremacy.

cards.title: Declaration of Independence USA
facts: The Thirteen Colonies declared independence from Great Britain.
This document proclaimed natural rights and government by consent.

cards.title: French Revolution
facts: The French Revolution began with the storming of the Bastille.
It led to the end of absolute monarchy in France.

cards.title: Battle of Austerlitz
facts: Napoleon defeated the combined armies of Austria and Russia.
It is considered one of Napoleon's greatest tactical victories.

cards.title: Congress of Vienna
facts: European powers redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon's defeat.
It aimed to restore balance of power and prevent future wars.

cards.title: Battle of Waterloo
facts: Napoleon was defeated by Allied forces led by the Duke of Wellington.
This ended the Napoleonic Wars and Napoleon's rule.

cards.title: Civil War US
facts: The American Civil War began between the Union and Confederate states.
It was fought primarily over slavery and states' rights.

cards.title: Begin of World War 1
facts: World War I began after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
It involved most of the world's great powers and lasted until 1918.

cards.title: October Revolution
facts: The Bolsheviks, led by Vladimir Lenin, seized power in Russia.
This led to the creation of the Soviet Union.

cards.title: Contract of Versailles
facts: The Treaty of Versailles officially ended World War I.
It imposed harsh penalties on Germany and redrew European borders.

cards.title: Spanish Flu
facts: The 1918-1919 influenza pandemic infected one-third of the world's population.
It killed an estimated 50 million people worldwide.

cards.title: Black Thursday
facts: The Wall Street stock market crash marked the beginning of the Great Depression.
It caused widespread economic hardship across the world.

cards.title: Start World War 2
facts: World War II began when Germany invaded Poland.
It was the deadliest conflict in human history, lasting until 1945.

cards.title: First UN Assembly
facts: The first General Assembly of the United Nations convened in London.
It marked the beginning of international cooperation after World War II.

cards.title: Foundation of the State of Israel
cards.image: Foundation of the State of Israel - 1948
facts: The State of Israel was proclaimed by David Ben-Gurion.
This followed the end of the British Mandate for Palestine.

cards.title: Establishment of NATO
facts: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization was formed as a military alliance.
It was created to counter the Soviet Union during the Cold War.

cards.title: Communist Revolution and Foundation of China
cards.image: Kommunist Revolution and Foundation of China - 1949
facts: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China.
This established communist rule in mainland China.

cards.title: Building of the Berlin Wall
facts: East Germany built the Berlin Wall to prevent citizens from fleeing to the West.
It became a symbol of the Cold War division.

cards.title: Prague Spring
facts: Alexander Dubček attempted to liberalize Czechoslovakia.
The reform movement was crushed by Warsaw Pact invasion.

cards.title: German Reunion
facts: East and West Germany reunified after the fall of the Berlin Wall.
This marked the end of Cold War division in Europe.

cards.title: End of Perestroika
facts: The Soviet Union officially dissolved, ending the Cold War.
This marked the collapse of communist rule in Eastern Europe.

cards.title: Foundation of the European Union (Maastricht)
facts: The Maastricht Treaty established the European Union.
It created the framework for economic and political integration in Europe.

cards.title: End of Apartheid in South Africa
facts: Nelson Mandela became the first Black president of South Africa.
This marked the end of institutionalized racial segregation.

cards.title: UK Leaves the EU (Brexit)
facts: The United Kingdom officially left the European Union.
This followed a 2016 referendum in which 52% voted to leave.

cards.title: COVID Pandemic
facts: The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally, causing widespread illness and death.
It led to lockdowns, economic disruption, and social changes worldwide.
